versionEvidence: New Border highlight, Shadows and GPU timing controls and corresponding Frame profile/House perf fields were observed. The exact Windows checkout SHA was not independently read.

conditions.view: Workshop approach, player idle, easel border active in baseline
conditions.method: Each sequential condition resets readings and excludes two-second warm-up, then collects five roughly three-second windows during a browser-control call. Baseline is repeated before the shadow/resolution tests and after resolution is restored. CPU profiler/logging stays enabled; one condition disables GPU timing.

summaryDefinition: FPS, CPU ms, GPU ms and callback interval entries summarize medians of five window-level values. GPU ms uses each renderer window's mean sampled GPU duration. gpuP95Ms is the median of window p95 values, not a pooled percentile.
observations: All seven conditions report 29 median FPS. Individual windows occasionally fell to 19-20 FPS; raw readings retain these outliers.
Baseline GPU window means have medians 16.52, 16.54 and 16.63 ms across the three baseline runs. Callback CPU medians are 7.25, 5.91 and 6.82 ms.
Border off removes one submitted draw and 16,672 submitted triangles, and reports 16.03 ms median GPU window mean. This is roughly 0.5 ms below adjacent baselines without a median FPS change.
Shadows off produces no meaningful GPU/FPS improvement in this view and preview hour; it does not measure the cost of all shadowed scenes.
DPR 0.55 reduces median sampled GPU window mean to 5.29 ms from the native 16.5-16.6 ms range. Median FPS remains 29 and callback interval median remains about 34.5 ms.
GPU timing disabled retains 29 median FPS, 6.66 ms median callback CPU and about 34.7 ms callback intervals. GPU durations correctly become null with disabled status.
The six GPU-enabled conditions produce 254 completed samples, ready status, no disjoint events, and at most one pending query in the captured reporting windows.
No 30 FPS limiter was found in the inspected Game/VisibleAnimationLoop scheduling path; it forwards visible frames to Three.js setAnimationLoop.
No error-level browser logs were observed. Startup warnings include unmatched finger animation tracks and unrelated extension locator warnings.
interpretation: At reduced resolution, shorter sampled GPU durations and short measured callback CPU work do not produce shorter callback intervals. This makes frame scheduling or work outside the measured callback the next investigation. It does not establish a browser frame cap, GPU utilization percentage, display refresh rate, Energy Saver state, or a specific driver/OS cause. CPU and GPU durations overlap and must not be added/subtracted as a frame budget.
limitations: One camera and preview hour; sequential short runs with changing browser/device load.
Browser automation and diagnostic logging remain active. No fresh Chrome Performance trace, display configuration, OS power/thermal data or uninstrumented comparison was captured.
The profiler covers Game callback work and sampled scene rendering, not DOM compositing, presentation, all browser work or OS scheduling.
Chrome internal settings navigation was blocked by browser security policy; no attempt was made to work around the restriction. Energy Saver remains unverified.
First-load/covered entry latency and long-session stability remain unmeasured.

restoredScreenshot.note: Viewport 1745x828 was read after baseline A3; dimensions were not independently read for every run. The later restored-settings screenshot has a different height.
